newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PMP SAYS ALL AREAS TRADING ABOVE 96/97 LEVELS.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PMP SAYS ALL AREAS TRADING ABOVE 96/97 LEVELS.

text.p: Australian multi-media publisher PMP Communications Ltd on Tuesday said all its businesses, after a flat first few weeks of the 1997/98 (July/June) year, were now trading above the same time last year.
PMP also said it expected its magazine publishing division to report a material rise in profit for 1997/98.
"The first couple of weeks were very flat, now we are trading above last year, progressively above last year," manging director Ken Catlow told an analysts briefing.
Asked how widespread was this improvement, Catlow said, "In every segment."
PMP finance director David Skelton told the briefing that profits from the publishing division alone would benefit substantially by the decision to cut back on new magazine launches this year.
"We would actually see a fairly material increase in earnings coming out of the publishing division...," Skelton said.
"We are talking at least A$4.5 million, which is 10 percent of current year (1996/97) earnings which will flow through on the basis of that," he said.
The company, which was 40 percent-owned by News Corp Ltd until early last month, on Tuesday said 1996/97 net profit fell to A$47.71 million from A$58.04 million.
News Corp offloaded its stake to a variety of investors.
